questions.q: Which is the correct way to compute a team win rate in a grouped report?
options: Take the highest rep's win rate
Divide the summed Won indicator by RowCount in a summary formula
Use a row-level formula that returns 1 or 0 and stop
questions.explain: Dividing summed values is a ratio of sums, which weights each rep by volume and stays correct on the grand total.

questions.q: Which function gives you the total from a higher grouping level so you can compute share of total?
questions.explain: PARENTGROUPVAL fetches a value from a higher grouping level, for example the grand summary, as the denominator for share of total.

questions.q: A share-of-total formula is set to display at all summary levels. What problem shows up on the grand total row?
options: It changes to a text value
It trivially reads 100 percent, so set the display level to groups only
questions.explain: The grand total divided by itself is always 100 percent. Restrict the formula's display level to the group levels where it means something.

questions.q: Which of these belongs in a row-level formula rather than a summary formula?
options: Amount multiplied by Probability for each opportunity before summing
Share of grand total by stage
Change from the previous month's total
questions.explain: Weighting each record before summing is a per-record calculation. The other three depend on aggregates or grouping structure.

questions.q: When PREVGROUPVAL is used on a report grouped by month, what should you expect for the first month?
options: A blank or zero, because there is no previous group
questions.explain: The first group has no predecessor, so the previous-value result is blank or zero. Guard any division that uses it.
